name: Opus-fleet price momentum
strategy: Concentrated long-only US price momentum rotated out of the broken memory/AI-hardware and rate-sensitive biotech themes and into the only complex actually printing new 52-week highs into 2026-09-15 - refining and the crude/product squeeze - with a secondary sleeve in the hardware-to-software rotation leaders, trend-break stops on every leg.
reassessment_note: The tape moved under my strategy of record. Of the four themes I owned into 2026-09-08, two are now confirmed downtrends and one has stalled. Memory/AI hardware has topped outright: MU is -22.9% off its 52w high and -14.0% over 3m, and the wider complex is worse (SNDK -26% 3m, WDC -36%, STX -24%, MRVL -27%, CRDO -41%, ALAB -33%, SMH -15%). The news flow matches the price - AI pacing/safety concerns are hammering chips while software rebounds. Taiwan semis via EWT is +0.7% over 3m, i.e. dead money in the same theme. Biotech has broken at the small-cap end: XBI -4.9% on the week and back below its 50dma, AMGN -15.2% off its high and -9.3% over 1m. TGT is soft with $103 crude and a 5.00% 10-year squeezing the consumer. Holding those five legs would mean running a momentum book on names that no longer have momentum, so they are cut. What is working is not ambiguous. Crude is $103.57, +11.3% on the week and +25.7% on the month; heating oil is +16.8% on the month and +53% over 3m; the SPR is at its lowest since 1982. Refiners are the direct beneficiary and every major is closing at a 52-week high today: VLO +14.3% 1m, MPC +13.5%, PSX +12.2%, DINO +17.2%, with CVI +45% and DK +16% confirming the breadth of the move. Tankers (FRO, STNG, INSW, DHT) are all at 52w highs too, which is the cross-asset confirmation that this is a physical dislocation and not a paper squeeze. I am therefore raising energy from 34% to 55% of the book and adding XLE as less-extended ballast plus two tanker legs. The remaining 35% goes to the actual non-energy leaders: MSFT (+25.5% 3m, +9.5% over its 50dma) and META (+9.2% on the week) as the hardware-to-software rotation winners, AAPL, DELL (kept - it is the one AI-hardware name still at a 52w high, +5.5% today post-earnings), and ABBV as large-cap pharma that is 2.8% off its high and far less rate-sensitive than the XBI I am selling. Event risk is explicit and I am sizing for it: with oil +26% on the month and the 10-year at 5.00%, the 2026-09-16 FOMC is being framed as a possible HIKE, not a cut. That is precisely why the rate-sensitive legs (XBI, AMGN, small caps, gold-adjacent) go and why the hard-asset legs stay. The refiners are 17-19% above their 50dmas and genuinely extended, so stops are set at 14% - wide enough to survive a normal shakeout in a 60%-a-quarter trend, tight enough that a real trend break takes me out. Churn cost on the ~60% of the book being replaced is roughly 2-3bps, immaterial against legs that are 14-23% below their highs.

positions.thesis: Closed at a 52-week high today (+2.0%), +14.3% over 1m, +58.0% over 3m, +140% over 12m - its best run since 1982 - and sits 18.5% above its 50dma with the trend still accelerating rather than rolling. Valero is the purest listed expression of the tight global refined-product market driving this move: Gulf Coast complexity means it captures the distillate crack that is up 53% over 3m. Largest single leg because it is the highest-conviction new-high name in the entire screen, and it is already in the book so I pay no round-trip to keep it.

Strongest 3-month refining momentum of the majors at +60.8% and +76.2% over 6m, closing at a 52-week high today, 19.3% above its 50dma. Marathon has the largest US refining system by throughput, so it carries the most absolute leverage to the crack widening, and its MPLX stake gives a midstream cash-flow floor if crude backs off. Held at near-max refining weight as the second core leg of the theme.

At a 52-week high, +12.2% 1m and +51.3% 3m, 16.7% above its 50dma - the least-extended of the three integrated refiners I hold, which is why it takes the smaller of the three core weights. Its midstream and chemicals segments dilute pure crack leverage slightly, so it functions as the lower-beta member of the refining sleeve while still participating in the trend.

New addition. At a 52-week high with +17.2% over 1m - faster than any of VLO/MPC/PSX - and +63.3% 3m, +94.0% 6m. HF Sinclair is a mid-continent refiner whose inland crude sourcing gives it a wider realized margin than coastal peers when WTI-linked feedstock lags the product move, so it is the highest-torque way to add refining exposure without doubling down on a name I already own. Slightly wider stop than the majors to respect the higher single-name volatility.

New addition as deliberate ballast inside the energy theme. XLE closed at a 52-week high but is only 7.9% above its 50dma versus 17-19% for my refining legs, so it carries the same directional trend at roughly half the extension. It also shifts part of my energy weight from crack-spread dependence to producers (XOM, CVX both at or near highs), which is the exposure that survives if product margins mean-revert while crude stays bid. Tight 10% stop because a diversified ETF that breaks 10% has broken the theme.

New addition. Product tanker rates are the physical confirmation of the refined-product dislocation: STNG closed at a 52-week high, +9.2% 1m, and sits only 10.2% above its 50dma - the cleanest, least-parabolic entry in the tanker group. Owning the shipping leg means I profit from the product imbalance itself rather than from any one refiner's margin capture. Small weight and a wide 18% stop because tanker equities routinely draw down 15% inside an intact uptrend.

New addition, smallest energy leg. Frontline is the fastest-moving name on the entire board at +12.7% on the week and +27.5% on the month, at a 52-week high, and VLCC rates are the highest-beta claim on crude being physically moved. It is 26.8% above its 50dma, which is parabolic, so it gets a 3% weight and a 20% stop - I want the convexity if the squeeze extends and a capped loss if it snaps.

New addition and the largest non-energy leg. +25.5% over 3m and +9.5% above its 50dma while QQQ is -4.7% over 3m and SMH is -15.4% - that is textbook relative-strength leadership, not beta. The specific driver is the rotation the tape is running right now: as AI-pacing concerns hammer chips, capital is moving into the software and cloud layer that monetizes AI without owning the capex cycle. Sized at 10% as the cleanest way to stay long the AI complex from the side that is still making progress.

The one AI-hardware position I keep, and the reason is purely price: it closed 0.65% off its 52-week high, +5.5% today, +14.8% 1m and +260% 6m, while every memory and networking peer I screened is 24-49% off its high. Post-earnings breakouts that hold while the whole peer group breaks are the strongest momentum signal available. Trimmed from 8% to 7% because theme-level guilt by association is a real risk, and the 18% stop reflects its realized volatility.

New addition on a fresh momentum inflection: +9.2% on the week and +13.6% on the month, the best 1-month print in mega-cap tech, turning up out of a base after a weak 12 months. It is still 14.1% below its 52-week high, so this is early-stage trend rather than a chase, and it is 10.9% above its 50dma confirming the turn is real. Sized at 6% precisely because the base is unproven relative to my energy legs.

New addition. +8.1% 1m, +11.6% 3m, and only 2.76% off its 52-week high - a steady, low-drawdown uptrend at a moment when the rest of large-cap tech is choppy. Apple has minimal AI-capex exposure, so it does not share the chip complex's downside, and its cash generation makes it relatively indifferent to a hawkish Fed. It is the lowest-volatility momentum leg available, hence the tight 10% stop.

New addition and the direct replacement for the XBI/AMGN biotech sleeve I am cutting. ABBV is +16.7% over 3m and only 2.75% off its 52-week high, versus XBI 9.1% off its high and below its 50dma and AMGN 15.2% off its high. Large-cap pharma with near-term cash flows is far less duration-sensitive than unprofitable small-cap biotech, which matters specifically because the 2026-09-16 FOMC is being priced for a hike with the 10-year at 5.00%. Keeps the healthcare exposure that is working and drops the part that is not.
